title: Photosynthesis
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Photosynthesis Worksheets (PSLE Practice with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise that green plants make food by photosynthesis, using light energy, water and carbon dioxide, with chlorophyll to trap light, and give out oxygen. Recognise that the Sun is the source of energy for plants and that the energy is stored in food. Investigate the factors that affect the rate of photosynthesis (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets on photosynthesis for Singapore pupils: what plants need, sugar and oxygen, chlorophyll, respiration and PSLE-style experiments. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants make food using light energy.
key_sub: Light, water and carbon dioxide go in; sugar and oxygen come out.
body_html:
How to think about it

Green plants make their own food. This is called photosynthesis.

  • They need light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll.
  • They make sugar (food) and give out oxygen.
  • It happens in the green parts, mostly the leaves. Chlorophyll traps light energy and the energy is stored in the food.
  • Plants also respire all the time, day and night.

water + carbon dioxide → sugar + oxygen (light energy, chlorophyll)

Example

A water plant gives off more bubbles when a lamp is moved nearer. Why?

More light reaches the plant

It makes food faster and gives off more oxygen

Answer: More light speeds up photosynthesis.

Example

Part of a leaf is covered with black paper. Which part has starch?

The covered part gets no light

It cannot make food

Answer: Only the uncovered part.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil. Soil gives water and minerals, not food.
  • Mixing up the gases: plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen when they make food.
  • Thinking plants respire only at night. They respire all the time.
  • Thinking the white parts of a leaf can make food. They have no chlorophyll.

faq.q: What do plants need for photosynthesis?
faq.a: Light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll. Water comes from the roots and carbon dioxide from the air.
Yes. Plants respire all the time, day and night, just like animals. In bright light they make food faster than they use it, so they give out oxygen overall.

faq.q: Why do water plants give off more bubbles near a lamp?
faq.a: Brighter light makes photosynthesis faster, so the plant gives off more oxygen. The bubbles are oxygen.

items.q: Which of these is NOT needed for photosynthesis?
items.e: Oxygen is given out, not taken in, during photosynthesis.

items.q: Which part of a plant carries the food made in the leaves to other parts?
items.e: Food-carrying tubes carry sugar all over the plant.

items.q: Which gas does a plant give out when it makes food?
items.e: Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen.

items.q: What does chlorophyll do in a leaf?
items.e: Chlorophyll is the green substance that traps light energy.

items.q: What food does a plant make during photosynthesis?
items.e: Plants make sugar. Some of it is stored as starch.

items.q: A cactus has no proper leaves. Which part of it makes food?
items.e: Green stems also have chlorophyll, so they can make some food.

items.q: A plant makes food by photosynthesis. Which of these does it need?
items.e: A plant needs light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll to make food. It does not need darkness to make food.

items.q: A plant makes food by photosynthesis. Which of these does it need?
items.e: A plant needs light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll to make food. It does not need sugar to make food.

items.q: A plant has carbon dioxide, chlorophyll and light. What else does it need to make food?
items.e: The four things needed for photosynthesis are light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll.

items.q: What is photosynthesis?
c: the way plants take in food from the soil
the way green plants make food using light energy
items.e: Photo means light; synthesis means making.

items.q: Why is photosynthesis important to animals?
c: It removes all oxygen from the air.
It makes the food and oxygen that animals need.
items.e: Animals eat plants (or eat animals that ate plants) and breathe in oxygen.

items.q: Which part of most plants makes the most food?
items.e: They are green and flat, so they trap the most light.

items.q: Which of these does a plant need to make food?
items.e: A plant needs light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll to make food. It does not need oxygen to make food.

items.q: A plant has light, carbon dioxide and water. What else does it need to make food?
items.e: The four things needed for photosynthesis are light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll.

items.q: Where does the carbon dioxide for photosynthesis come from?
items.e: It enters the leaves through tiny openings.

items.q: How does water reach the leaves to make food?
c: Leaves take it in from the air.
Roots take it in and the water-carrying tubes carry it up.
It is made in the flowers.
items.e: Water travels from the roots up the stem to the leaves.

items.q: What happens to sugar that a plant does not use straight away?
c: It is given out through the roots.
items.e: Starch is stored in leaves, stems, roots, fruits and seeds.

items.q: What is the source of energy for photosynthesis?
items.e: Usually sunlight.

items.q: Where does a plant get its food?
c: It takes food from the soil.
It makes the food itself in its green parts.
items.e: Soil gives water and minerals, but not food.

items.q: A plant has chlorophyll, water and carbon dioxide. What else does it need to make food?
items.e: The four things needed for photosynthesis are light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll.

items.q: Where in a plant is most sugar made?
items.e: Leaves have the most chlorophyll and get the most light.

items.q:
What is missing from the word equation for photosynthesis?
? + carbon dioxide ——[light, chlorophyll]——> sugar + oxygen
items.e: water + carbon dioxide → sugar + oxygen, using light energy, with chlorophyll to trap the light.

items.q: Which part of a leaf lets carbon dioxide in?
c: tiny openings on the leaf surface
items.e: Gases move in and out through tiny openings (stomata), mostly on the underside of the leaf.

items.q: Why are leaves green?
items.e: Chlorophyll gives the green colour.

items.q: Why does sugar cane taste sweet?
c: It takes in sugar from the soil.
Its stem stores the sugar made in the leaves.
items.e: Food made in the leaves is carried to the stem and stored.

items.q: What is the stored food in a seed used for?
c: to help the young plant grow until it can make its own food
items.e: A seedling uses stored food until its leaves can photosynthesise.

items.q:
What is missing from the word equation for photosynthesis?
water + ? ——[light, chlorophyll]——> sugar + oxygen
items.e: water + carbon dioxide → sugar + oxygen, using light energy, with chlorophyll to trap the light.

items.q: Which energy change happens during photosynthesis?
c: light energy to chemical potential energy
sound energy to chemical potential energy
chemical potential energy to light energy
items.e: Plants change light energy into energy stored in food.

items.q: A cow eats grass. Where did the energy in the grass first come from?
items.e: Plants trap light energy from the Sun and store it in the food they make. Animals get this energy by eating plants.

items.q: Which form of energy is stored in the food a plant makes?
items.e: Light energy is changed into chemical potential energy.

items.q: A bird eats a ripe papaya. The energy in the papaya was first trapped by which part of the papaya tree?
items.e: Leaves trap light energy from the Sun and the food made there is stored in the fruit.

items.q:
What is missing from the word equation for photosynthesis?
water + carbon dioxide ——[light, chlorophyll]——> ? + oxygen
items.e: water + carbon dioxide → sugar + oxygen, using light energy, with chlorophyll to trap the light.

items.q: Which statement about photosynthesis and respiration is correct?
c: Photosynthesis makes food; respiration uses food to release energy.
Respiration makes food; photosynthesis uses it.
items.e: They work in opposite directions.

items.q: Which living things can make their own food?
items.e: Only things with chlorophyll can make food by photosynthesis. Fungi such as mushrooms cannot.

items.q: Which of these plants stores food in its root?
items.e: A carrot is a swollen root. Sugar cane stores sugar in its stem.

items.q: What does photosynthesis do with light energy?
c: It releases it as heat only.
items.e: Light energy is changed into chemical potential energy in sugar.

items.q: A caterpillar eats leaves to get energy. Where does all of this energy start?
items.e: Plants trap light energy from the Sun; the caterpillar gets it by eating the leaves.

items.q: A leaf turned blue-black when iodine was added. What does this show?
items.e: Iodine turns blue-black with starch.

items.q: Which fruit stores food that was made in the leaves?
c: none, fruits make their own food
items.e: Food-carrying tubes carry sugar from the leaves to the fruits.

items.q: In which part of a potato plant is food stored?
items.e: A potato is a swollen underground stem that stores starch.

items.q: Both sides of a leaf on a spinach plant were covered with Vaseline. Why did the leaf stop making food?
c: Carbon dioxide could not get into the leaf.
Light could not reach the leaf.
Water could not leave the leaf.
items.e: Vaseline blocks the tiny openings, so carbon dioxide cannot get in. Light still passes through.

items.q: When does a plant respire?
c: all the time, day and night
items.e: All living things respire all the time to release energy.

items.q: Why does a plant need oxygen?
c: for respiration, to release energy from food
items.e: Plants use oxygen to respire, like animals.

items.q:
Two hibiscus plants were kept in sunlight (A) and in the dark (B). Both were watered.
PlantMass at start (g)Mass after 2 weeks (g)
A (in sunlight)5060
B (in the dark)5046
Why did plant B lose mass?
c: It could not make food but still used up food to respire.
It took in too much carbon dioxide.
items.e: In the dark there is no photosynthesis, but respiration uses up stored food all the time.

items.q: At night, which gas does a plant give out?
items.e: There is no light at night, so there is no photosynthesis. The plant still respires and gives out carbon dioxide.

items.q: On a sunny afternoon, which gas does a healthy plant give out the most?
items.e: In bright light, photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so the plant gives out oxygen overall.

items.q: Two identical spinach plants were kept for a week, one in normal air and one in air with the carbon dioxide removed. Everything else was the same. What was being tested?
c: whether carbon dioxide is needed for a plant to make food
whether the plant needs oxygen to make food
whether the plant can grow flowers
items.e: Only one thing was different between the two plants: carbon dioxide.

items.q: On a sunny afternoon, which gas does a healthy plant take in the most?
items.e: In bright light, the plant uses carbon dioxide to make food faster than respiration makes it.

items.q: Two identical balsam plants were kept for a week, one in light and one in the dark. Everything else was the same. What was being tested?
c: whether light is needed for a plant to make food
whether the plant can grow flowers
whether the plant needs oxygen to make food
items.e: Only one thing was different between the two plants: light.

items.q: A mouse and a green plant were kept in a sealed jar in sunlight. Why did the mouse live longer than a mouse kept alone?
c: The plant made the jar darker.
The plant gave off carbon dioxide.
The plant gave off oxygen for the mouse.
The plant was food for the mouse.
items.e: The plant takes in the mouse's carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen in light.

items.q: Limewater turns chalky when there is a lot of carbon dioxide. A jar with a plant in the dark had limewater in it. What happened?
items.e: The plant respired and gave out carbon dioxide, but could not use it without light.

items.q: A plant was kept in a sealed glass jar on a sunny windowsill. What happened to the amount of oxygen in the jar during the day?
items.e: In bright light the plant gives off more oxygen than it uses.

items.q: Which gas do both plants and animals give out when they respire?
items.e: Respiration uses oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide.

items.q: At night, which gas does a plant take in?
items.e: At night the plant only respires: it takes in oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide.

items.q: Two identical balsam plants were kept for a week, one watered and one not watered. Everything else was the same. Which plant made more food?
items.e: Water is needed for photosynthesis.

items.q: Part of a leaf on a rain tree seedling was covered with black paper and left in sunlight for a day. Which part had starch?
items.e: The covered part got no light, so it could not make food.

items.q: Why are green plants called food producers?
c: They take food from the soil.
They make their own food using light energy.
items.e: Animals depend on the food plants make.

items.q: At dawn, the light is very dim. Which statement is most likely true?
c: The plant makes food very fast.
The plant makes very little food but still respires.
The plant gives out only oxygen.
items.e: Little light means slow photosynthesis; respiration goes on all the time.

items.q: Why do some people say there is fresh air in a park with many trees?
c: The trees take in oxygen in the day.
The trees give off oxygen in the day.
The trees give off carbon dioxide in the day.
Trees make the air colder only.
items.e: Trees photosynthesise in sunlight and release oxygen.

items.q: A plant was kept in a sealed glass jar in a dark room. What happened to the amount of carbon dioxide in the jar?
items.e: In the dark the plant only respires and gives out carbon dioxide.

items.q: Which leaf would make the most food on a sunny day?
c: a white leaf at the top of the plant
a leaf covered with black paper
a large green leaf at the top of the plant
a small leaf in the shade
items.e: It has chlorophyll and gets the most light.

items.q: Before an experiment, a bean plant was kept in the dark for 2 days. Why?
c: to use up the starch already in its leaves
items.e: Then any starch found later must have been made during the experiment.

items.q: Why should the two plants in an experiment be of the same type and size?
c: so that they make more oxygen
so that they need less water
so that the test is fair
items.e: Only the variable being tested should be different.

items.q: Two identical chilli plants were kept for a week, one watered and one not watered. Everything else was the same. What was being tested?
c: whether the plant can grow flowers
whether the plant needs oxygen to make food
whether water is needed for a plant to make food
items.e: Only one thing was different between the two plants: water.

items.q: Hui Min wants to find out if the amount of light affects how fast a plant makes food. What should she change?
items.e: Change only the variable you are testing.

items.q: A money plant has leaves with green and white parts. After a sunny day, which parts of a leaf have starch?
items.e: The white parts have no chlorophyll, so they cannot trap light to make food.

items.q: A plant was kept in sunlight with one leaf in a bag with a chemical that removes carbon dioxide. Why did that leaf have no starch?
c: It had no carbon dioxide to make food.
items.e: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis.

items.q: Two identical spinach plants were kept for a week, one in normal air and one in air with the carbon dioxide removed. Everything else was the same. Which plant made more food?
c: the plant in air with the carbon dioxide removed
items.e: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis.

items.q: Ahmad kept a pandan plant in a dark cupboard for 3 days, then tested a leaf for starch. What did Ahmad find?
items.e: With no light, the plant cannot make food, and it uses up the starch it had.

items.q: Why do plants on the forest floor often have large, wide leaves?
c: to trap as much of the little light there as possible
items.e: Bigger leaves trap more light where it is shady.

items.q: Two identical bean plants were kept for a week, one in light and one in the dark. Everything else was the same. Which plant made more food?
items.e: Light is needed for photosynthesis.

items.q: Why is a control set-up used in a plant experiment?
c: to use up the plant's starch
to give the plant more light
to compare with the set-up that has one thing changed
to make the plant grow faster
items.e: The control shows what happens when nothing is changed.

items.q: A spinach plant was placed in a box with a hole on one side. After a week, it grew towards the hole. Why is this useful?
c: It gets more light to make food.
items.e: Plants grow towards light so their leaves can make more food.

items.q: Siti grew one plant under a red lamp and one under a green lamp of the same brightness. The red-lamp plant grew more. What was she testing?
c: how the colour of light affects how a plant makes food
how the size of the pot affects growth
items.e: Only the colour of light was changed.

items.q: Jun Jie says plants make food only for themselves. Why is he wrong?
c: Food made by plants cannot be eaten.
Animals that eat plants also get the food and energy the plants stored.
Animals make their own food too.
items.e: Plants are at the start of every food chain.

items.q: Ahmad covered the top of a pot of soil with plastic so no water could evaporate, then weighed a plant over a sunny day. Why did the plant's mass go up a little at the end of the week?
c: It absorbed oxygen from the air.
It made food and stored it, so it grew.
items.e: Food made by photosynthesis is used to grow.

items.q: A pot plant was watered with water containing a coloured dye. Where would the dye be found first?
items.e: Water moves up from the roots through water-carrying tubes.

items.q: A plant with its leaves removed was kept in sunlight. Why did it stop growing?
c: It could not take in water.
It gave out too much oxygen.
It could not make food without leaves.
items.e: Leaves are where most food is made.

items.q: A fish tank has water plants and fish. Why do the water plants help the fish?
c: They give off oxygen that the fish need.
items.e: Plants add oxygen to the water when they make food in light.

items.q: Why are crops in greenhouses sometimes given extra carbon dioxide?
c: to help them make food faster
items.e: More carbon dioxide can speed up photosynthesis.
